User GuideAI-GENERATED

Serves for the ordered management of unique key-value pairs with configurable allocator support.
AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: ce48c351c6cf Provenance

Serves for the ordered management of unique key-value pairs with configurable allocator support.

The associative key-value container ara::core::Map implements std::pmr::map and manages sorted entries based on unique keys using polymorphic allocators ([SWS_CORE_01404]). Applications use the container for structured insertion, search, and removal of data pairs as well as for efficient node transfer using move semantics. As an essential peculiarity, indexed access via at triggers an IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation instead of the standard exception in the case of missing keys ([SWS_CORE_01456]). While status queries are exception-safe, dynamic memory allocations during insertion require appropriate precautions against resource shortages.

Context

The template class ara::core::Map provides an ordered associative key-value container that conforms to the semantics of std::pmr::map from the C++ standard. Keys of type key_type ([SWS_CORE_01402]) are unique and sorted based on a predicate of type key_compare ([SWS_CORE_01405]). The data pairs are managed as value_type in the form of std::pair<const Key, T> ([SWS_CORE_01404]). The primary interaction partner is the applying software component of the Adaptive Platform, which can selectively integrate user-defined or polymorphic memory allocators via the configurable allocator_type ([SWS_CORE_01406]).

Lifecycle

The instantiation of ara::core::Map can take place via the default constructor ([SWS_CORE_01428]), with specification of allocators ([SWS_CORE_01431]), or with comparison objects ([SWS_CORE_01429]). In addition, constructors for iterator ranges ([SWS_CORE_01430], [SWS_CORE_01435]) and initializer lists ([SWS_CORE_01434], [SWS_CORE_01436]) are available. The copy constructor ([SWS_CORE_01424]) and copy assignment operator ([SWS_CORE_01425]) are specified as default, but are supplemented by allocator-specific overloads ([SWS_CORE_01432]).

For efficient resource transfer, move constructors exist ([SWS_CORE_01426], [SWS_CORE_01433]). The move assignment operator ([SWS_CORE_01427]) offers conditional exception safety, provided that std::allocator_traits<Allocator>::is_always_equal::value and std::is_nothrow_move_assignable<Compare>::value are satisfied. When destroying the container via the destructor ([SWS_CORE_01437]), all contained nodes are released. Swapping two instances via swap ([SWS_CORE_01484]) uses the AUTOSAR predicate ara::core::is_nothrow_swappable for protection instead of the standard library.

Usage Path

Regular use includes inserting, finding, reading, and clearing entries:

  • Insert and update: New pairs can be constructed by means of emplace ([SWS_CORE_01458]) or try_emplace ([SWS_CORE_01472], [SWS_CORE_01473]) without unnecessary temporary objects. In addition, insert ([SWS_CORE_01460]) and insert_or_assign ([SWS_CORE_01476]) allow adding or overwriting. The index operator operator[] ([SWS_CORE_01454], [SWS_CORE_01455]) creates missing entries implicitly.
  • Search and range queries: The existence of a key is checked via contains ([SWS_CORE_01510]) or count ([SWS_CORE_01494]). Finding specific elements is carried out via find ([SWS_CORE_01490]), while lower_bound ([SWS_CORE_01498]) and equal_range ([SWS_CORE_01506]) access subranges. Iterations over all elements use begin ([SWS_CORE_01440]) and end ([SWS_CORE_01442]).
  • Removal and reorganization: Entries are removed via erase ([SWS_CORE_01480], [SWS_CORE_01482]) or completely erased via clear ([SWS_CORE_01485]). Advanced operations permit extracting individual nodes via extract ([SWS_CORE_01470]) or merging entire containers via merge ([SWS_CORE_01486]).

Sequence diagram: Typical flow of container operations in ara::core::Map from insertion to lookup to erasure. Sources: [SWS_CORE_01472], [SWS_CORE_01490], [SWS_CORE_01456], [SWS_CORE_01482].

Error Scenarios

A central deviation from the ISO C++ standard concerns the access method at ([SWS_CORE_01456], [SWS_CORE_01457]): If a requested key is not found in the container, the implementation does not throw an std::out_of_range exception, but triggers an IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation. Despite the signature with noexcept, the method signals this violation immediately; this is likely due to the platform-wide strategy of reporting errors in safety-relevant environments without classic C++ exceptions.

Capacity queries such as empty ([SWS_CORE_01511]), size ([SWS_CORE_01452]), or get_allocator ([SWS_CORE_01439]) are fully exception-safe (noexcept). In contrast, allocation and insertion operations such as insert ([SWS_CORE_01460]), emplace ([SWS_CORE_01458]), or the default constructors ([SWS_CORE_01428]) are classified as not exception safe, since exhaustion of the configured memory can lead to errors.

This class guide is based on the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform specification R25-11 for the core module and was generated automatically.

                                              function at [SWS_CORE_01456]
                                              

                                              mapped_type & at (const key_type &x) noexcept;
                                              

                                              As per corresponding usage in [map] except for the following deviations: 1. if (x is not found in the container) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std::out_of_range
                                              

                                              

                                              

                                              

                                              

                                              

                                              

                                              

                                              
  AI-GENERATED
  unreviewed
  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 91afb1d880dc
  Provenance
  

                                              

                                              

                                              use
                                              

                                              The synchronous element access function at of class ara::core::Map ([SWS_CORE_01456]) serves for controlled retrieval of a value for an existing key. It is provided via header ara/core/map.h. As input parameter, it accepts a key reference const key_type &x and returns a modifiable reference mapped_type & to the associated value ([SWS_CORE_01456]). The semantics fundamentally correspond to the customary usage of std::map; for const instances, separate overload [SWS_CORE_01457] is available.
                                              


                                              Error Handling and Boundary Conditions
                                              

                                              In case of error, the function deliberately deviates from standard ISO behavior: if the specified element x is not present in the container, a IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is triggered instead of a classic C++ exception of type std::out_of_range ([SWS_CORE_01456]). The signature is explicitly declared as noexcept and classified as exception safe (exception safe) ([SWS_CORE_01456]).
                                              


                                              Interaction
                                              

                                              The concept of indicating out-of-range errors via IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is implemented uniformly module-wide:
                                              

                                                

                                              • Within ara::core::Map, the read overload with const exhibits the same error behavior ([SWS_CORE_01457]).
                                                • 

                                              • Corresponding at functions with IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation exist for ara::core::Array ([SWS_CORE_01273], [SWS_CORE_01274]), ara::core::Vector ([SWS_CORE_01354], [SWS_CORE_01355]), ara::core::StringView ([SWS_CORE_02133]), and ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03063], [SWS_CORE_03064]).
                                                • 

                                              • The triggered violation is presumably related to abort and termination mechanisms such as AddAbortHandler ([SWS_CORE_00054]) in the overall system.
                                                • 

                                              


                                              

                                              This usage note was automatically generated based on specification R25-11.

                                                  function at [SWS_CORE_01457]
                                                  

                                                  const mapped_type & at (const key_type &x) const noexcept;
                                                  

                                                  As per corresponding usage in [map] except for the following deviations: 1. if (x is not found in the container) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std::out_of_range
                                                  

                                                  

                                                  

                                                  

                                                  

                                                  

                                                  

                                                  

                                                  
  AI-GENERATED
  unreviewed
  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 63bb4d175e4a
  Provenance
  

                                                  

                                                  

                                                  use
                                                  
  
                                                  The member function at according to [SWS_CORE_01457] enables synchronous, read-only access to an element within an instance of ara::core::Map via header #include "ara/core/map.h". As a parameter, the searched key x is passed as const key_type &. Upon successful lookup, the method returns a const reference to the associated value (const mapped_type &).
                                                  

  
                                                  Error Handling and Exception Behavior
                                                  
  
                                                  The behavior basically corresponds to the standard behavior of std::map::at, but exhibits a specific deviation: if the key x is not found in the container, a IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is thrown instead of std::out_of_range according to [SWS_CORE_01457]. Since the function is specified with noexcept, this violation does not lead to a regular C++ exception; presumably, this entails a controlled process termination via the error handling mechanisms as can be registered in the context of [SWS_CORE_00054].
                                                  

  
                                                  Concurrency and Interaction
                                                  
  
                                                  As a const method, the call qualifies for concurrent read access, provided that no concurrent modifying accesses to the same map instance take place. In addition to this const interface, a non-const overload exists with [SWS_CORE_01456], which returns a modifiable reference. The same strategy for signaling range violations using IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is consistently implemented in other adaptive core containers as well, for example with ara::core::Array ([SWS_CORE_01274]) and ara::core::Vector ([SWS_CORE_01354]).

                                                                      function clear [SWS_CORE_01485]
                                                                      

                                                                      void clear () noexcept;
                                                                      

                                                                      As per corresponding usage in [map]
                                                                      

                                                                      

                                                                      

                                                                      

                                                                      

                                                                      

                                                                      

                                                                      

                                                                      
  AI-GENERATED
  unreviewed
  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: caea3d46193b
  Provenance
  

                                                                      

                                                                      

                                                                      The member function clear of class ara::core::Map serves to completely clear the container content according to the specification in [SWS_CORE_01485]. The function requires including header file #include "ara/core/map.h". Call semantics and behavior follow the corresponding usage of the ISO C++ standard for associative standard maps ([map]).
                                                                      


                                                                      Regarding interface and error handling, the function exhibits the following properties:
                                                                      

                                                                        

                                                                      • Parameters and return value: The operation has the signature void clear () noexcept;, takes no parameters, and returns no value [SWS_CORE_01485].
                                                                        • 

                                                                      • Exception safety: The function is explicitly declared as noexcept and specified as exception safe [SWS_CORE_01485]. It thus throws no C++ exceptions in the event of an error.
                                                                        • 

                                                                      • Synchronous execution: The call is executed synchronously on the instance; after returning, the container is likely to be empty (size 0).
                                                                        • 

                                                                      


                                                                      In module core, clearing standard containers follows a uniform paradigm. Analogous clear functions with identical signature and exception safety are found, for example, for sequential containers in ara::core::Vector according to [SWS_CORE_01375] (ara/core/vector.h) and for strings in ara::core::BasicString according to [SWS_CORE_03057] (ara/core/string.h). Developers can rely across containers on the familiar standard C++ semantics and guaranteed freedom from exceptions.

                                                                          function contains [SWS_CORE_01497]
                                                                          

                                                                          template <class K> bool contains (const K &x) const;
                                                                          

                                                                          As per corresponding usage in [map]
                                                                          

                                                                          

                                                                          

                                                                          

                                                                          

                                                                          

                                                                          

                                                                          

                                                                          
  AI-GENERATED
  unreviewed
  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: ca604ba15c6f
  Provenance
  

                                                                          

                                                                          

                                                                          The template method contains of class ara::core::Map serves to synchronously check whether a searched key exists in an associative container [SWS_CORE_01497]. It is provided via the header #include "ara/core/map.h" and is called as a constant member function (const) on an instance of ara::core::Map [SWS_CORE_01497]. As a call parameter, it accepts a constant reference const K &x to the key to be searched and returns a return value of type bool [SWS_CORE_01497].
                                                                          

                                                                          Regarding its semantics, the specification refers to the corresponding usage in [map] [SWS_CORE_01497]. This is likely to be interpreted as adopting the behavior of std::map::contains, according to which the method returns true if and only if an equivalent key is contained in the map, and false otherwise.
                                                                          

                                                                          Regarding robustness and error handling, the function is explicitly classified as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_01497]. Specific AUTOSAR error codes or notifications to DET or DEM do not exist for this operation. Callers must take into account that during execution, presumably triggered by key comparisons or conversions of type K, exceptions can be thrown and propagated outward.
                                                                          

                                                                          Since contains, as a reading const operation, does not modify the state of the map, concurrent read accesses to the same instance are generally uncritical, whereas parallel write modifications to the container are likely to require external synchronization.

                                                                              function contains [SWS_CORE_01510]
                                                                              

                                                                              bool contains (const key_type &x) const;
                                                                              

                                                                              As per corresponding usage in [map]
                                                                              

                                                                              

                                                                              

                                                                              

                                                                              

                                                                              

                                                                              

                                                                              

                                                                              
  AI-GENERATED
  unreviewed
  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: cbd6e7493a69

                                                                              Usage and Semantics
                                                                              
  
                                                                              The member function contains belongs to the scope of class ara::core::Map and is provided via header file ara/core/map.h [SWS_CORE_01510]. The function has the signature bool contains (const key_type &x) const; and is executed synchronously. It serves to check whether an element with the key x is present in the container. The specification refers to the corresponding behavior in [map], which presumably means the semantics of the C++ standard container std::map::contains, which returns true if the key is present and false otherwise.
                                                                              

  
                                                                              Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                              
  
                                                                              The behavior of contains is explicitly classified in the specification as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_01510]. Specific error codes, error domains, and DET or DEM notifications are not defined in the scope of the specification. Callers must therefore take into account that no exception safety guarantees are granted during the search and that occurring exceptions must be handled.
                                                                              

  
                                                                              Concurrency and Limitations
                                                                              
  
                                                                              The specification makes no explicit statement regarding thread safety in [SWS_CORE_01510]. Because it is a const member function (const), the container state is not modified. Interpretation: Parallel read accesses are likely permissible, whereas concurrent write modifications to the same instance require external synchronization.
                                                                              

  
                                                                              Interaction in module core
                                                                              
  
                                                                              In comparison to other state-checking functions of module core \u2014 such as HasValue [SWS_CORE_00751] or CheckError [SWS_CORE_00765] in ara::core::Result, which are defined as exception safe and noexcept \u2014 contains in ara::core::Map provides no noexcept guarantee and is declared as not exception-safe [SWS_CORE_01510].

                                                                                  function count [SWS_CORE_01494]
                                                                                  

                                                                                  size_type count (const key_type &x) const;
                                                                                  

                                                                                  As per corresponding usage in [map]
                                                                                  

                                                                                  

                                                                                  

                                                                                  

                                                                                  

                                                                                  

                                                                                  

                                                                                  

                                                                                  
  AI-GENERATED
  unreviewed
  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 2a35e539f92e
  Provenance
  

                                                                                  

                                                                                  

                                                                                  The synchronous member function count of class ara::core::Map determines, based on the passed key x of type const key_type&, how often this key occurs in the container and returns the result as size_type [SWS_CORE_01494]. It is declared via header #include "ara/core/map.h" [SWS_CORE_01494]. Interpretation: Corresponding to the reference to the standard behavior in [map], the return value is likely to be either 0 or 1 in the case of unique keys.
                                                                                  

                                                                                  Regarding error handling, the function is expressly classified as “not exception safe” according to the specification [SWS_CORE_01494]. No specific error codes or DET/DEM messages are defined; if the key comparison operation throws an exception, it is presumably propagated directly to the caller.
                                                                                  

                                                                                  Regarding concurrency and limitations, this is a const operation (const) [SWS_CORE_01494]. Interpretation: Concurrent read accesses to the same instance of ara::core::Map are likely to be possible without data races, whereas simultaneous modifying operations must be secured by external synchronization.
                                                                                  

                                                                                  In interplay with related requirements, a template overload template <class K> size_type count (const K &x) const within ara::core::Map exists with [SWS_CORE_01495]. This enables heterogeneous search queries with compatible comparison types K without having to mandatorily construct a temporary object of type key_type beforehand, but is subject to the same classification regarding exception safety [SWS_CORE_01495].

The function is declared in header ara/core/map.h and returns the number of found elements as size_type [SWS_CORE_01495]. According to the specified reference to usage in [map], for unique keys the call returns the value 1 if a matching element exists, and 0 otherwise [SWS_CORE_01495].

Interpretation: The templating is likely designed for heterogeneous lookup operations in order to perform comparisons without prior conversion into a temporary key_type object [SWS_CORE_01495]. As a result, unnecessary allocations and conversion costs during search queries can be avoided.
                                                                                      

                                                                                      Regarding exception safety, the method is declared as not exception safe (not exception safe) [SWS_CORE_01495], analogously to the related overload [SWS_CORE_01494]. Specific error channels such as DET or DEM do not exist for this container operation [SWS_CORE_01495]; any exceptions of the underlying comparison operator propagate to the caller. Because the method is const-qualified, it does not modify the container [SWS_CORE_01495]; concurrent read accesses are safe, but competing write accesses require external synchronization.

It takes no parameters and synchronously returns a const_reverse_iterator to the first element of the reverse sequence [SWS_CORE_01450]. The functional semantics follow the specification statement “As per corresponding usage in [map]” [SWS_CORE_01450]; this presumably corresponds to the semantics of std::map::crbegin from the C++ standard.

Specific error codes, DET, or DEM messages are not provided for this call.                                                                                           Concurrency and Limitations
                                                                                          

                                                                                          
As a const-qualified method, crbegin does not modify the ara::core::Map object [SWS_CORE_01450]. The resulting iterator only permits read access to the elements contained in the container.

                                                                                              use
                                                                                              

                                                                                              The method crend of the template class ara::core::Map ([SWS_CORE_01451]) is available via header ara/core/map.h. It synchronously returns a constant reverse iterator (const_reverse_iterator) that, according to the standard behavior of std::map, marks the reaching of the end of a reverse iteration over the elements.
                                                                                              


                                                                                              Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                                              

                                                                                              The function has the specification noexcept and is classified as “exception safe” ([SWS_CORE_01451]). The call throws no exceptions and requires no checking of error codes.
                                                                                              


                                                                                              Concurrency and Constraints
                                                                                              

                                                                                              As a const-qualified method, crend does not modify the underlying map instance. Concurrent read accesses across multiple threads should therefore be safe as long as the instance is not concurrently modified by writing (interpretation).
                                                                                              


                                                                                              Interaction
                                                                                              

                                                                                              The signature and semantics fit into the uniform iterator interfaces of the ara::core library. Analogous crend functions exist for:
                                                                                              

                                                                                                

                                                                                              • ara::core::Vector ([SWS_CORE_01343]) and ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03050]), each with an identical const noexcept declaration, as well as
                                                                                                •

                                                                                                  Usage of emplace in ara::core::Map
                                                                                                  

                                                                                                  The template member function emplace of class ara::core::Map serves to directly construct and insert a new key-value pair into the associative container [SWS_CORE_01458]. The function is defined in header #include "ara/core/map.h" and receives constructor arguments via parameter pack Args&&... args [SWS_CORE_01458]. As a result, the synchronous call returns a std::pair<iterator, bool> [SWS_CORE_01458]. Interpretation: The reference to [map] likely means that the behavior follows the C++ standard container std::map, such that the iterator refers to the element and the boolean value indicates whether the entry was newly inserted.
                                                                                                  


                                                                                                  Regarding error handling and robustness, emplace is expressly classified in the specification as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_01458]. If memory allocation or object construction fails, the implementation does not guarantee container consistency. Specific AUTOSAR error codes or messages to DET or DEM are not provided for this fundamental interface.
                                                                                                  


                                                                                                  In module core, analogous emplace operations exist for other data types, which however possess different guarantees: While ara::core::Vector::emplace is also specified as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_01366], the implementations in ara::core::Optional [SWS_CORE_01119] and ara::core::Variant [SWS_CORE_01661] offer conditional exception safety (conditionally exception safe).

                                                                                                      Concurrency and Limitations
                                                                                                      

                                                                                                      The specification makes no statement regarding concurrency and call contexts ([SWS_CORE_01459]). Interpretation: As a state-modifying operation on ara::core::Map, emplace_hint requires external synchronization upon concurrent access by multiple threads to prevent data inconsistencies.

                                                                                                                      function equal_range [SWS_CORE_01506]
                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                      std::pair< iterator, iterator > equal_range (const key_type &x);
                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                      As per corresponding usage in [map]
                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                      
  AI-GENERATED
  unreviewed
  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: f0055ff4279d
  Provenance
  

                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                      use
                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                      The synchronous member function equal_range of class ara::core::Map is provided via header #include "ara/core/map.h" [SWS_CORE_01506]. It accepts a key x of type const key_type & and returns a pair of mutable iterators (std::pair<iterator, iterator>) that delimits the range of all matching entries [SWS_CORE_01506]. The behavior follows the usual semantics in [map] [SWS_CORE_01506]; since Map typically possesses unique keys, the resulting range is likely to comprise at most one element (interpretation).
                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                      Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                      The specification explicitly classifies the function as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_01506]. Specific error codes, return values for error signaling, or reports to DET or DEM are not defined. If the searched key is not found, both iterators of the pair are likely to be identical and point to the potential insertion position (interpretation according to [map]).
                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                      Concurrency and Limitations
                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                      The operation is non-const and returns non-const iterators [SWS_CORE_01506]. Since no synchronization mechanisms are documented, concurrent read or write accesses to the same instance of ara::core::Map are presumably not thread-safe (interpretation) and require external synchronization.
                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                      Interaction
                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                      For read accesses to const instances, the overload with const_iterator pairs is available [SWS_CORE_01507]. In addition, template variants exist for heterogeneous lookup operations with an arbitrary key type K, both for non-const calls [SWS_CORE_01508] and for const calls [SWS_CORE_01509].

                                                                                                                          use
                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                          The member function equal_range of class ara::core::Map determines the range of all entries matching a specified key on a const instance [SWS_CORE_01507]. It takes the parameter const key_type &x and returns a std::pair<const_iterator, const_iterator> that represents the bounds of the range [SWS_CORE_01507]. The function is provided via the header file ara/core/map.h and executed synchronously [SWS_CORE_01507]. The semantics correspond to the specification of [map] [SWS_CORE_01507]; accordingly, for a map with unique keys, the returned range is likely to cover a span of at most one entry.
                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                          Error Handling and Boundary Conditions
                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                          With regard to error and exception behavior, the method is specified as not exception safe (“not exception safe”) [SWS_CORE_01507]. No specific error codes, DET messages, or DEM events are defined. Because the method is declared as const, it does not modify the state of the calling object.
                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                          Interaction
                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                          The operation is embedded in a series of related overloads within ara::core::Map:
                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                            

                                                                                                                          • For non-const instances, [SWS_CORE_01506] offers the same search, but returns modifiable iterators.
                                                                                                                            • 

                                                                                                                          • Via the template functions [SWS_CORE_01508] and [SWS_CORE_01509], the search can also be performed with compatible keys of type K for mutable as well as const maps.

                                                                                                                              Usage and Semantics
                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                              The template member function equal_range of class ara::core::Map ([SWS_CORE_01508]) is provided via header ara/core/map.h. It serves to find the range of all elements whose key matches the passed value. The behavior follows the corresponding usage in [map] ([SWS_CORE_01508]). The synchronous call takes a key parameter x of generic type const K& and returns a std::pair<iterator, iterator> ([SWS_CORE_01508]) as return value. Interpretation: Through the generic parameter type K, the function is likely to support heterogeneous lookup, so that comparisons are possible without prior conversion to key_type.
                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                              Error Handling and Boundary Conditions
                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                              According to the specification, the function is classified as not exception safe (not exception safe) ([SWS_CORE_01508]). Specific error codes, return values for error indication, or messages to DET or DEM are not provided. Because the function is not qualified as const, it returns modifiable iterators that permit write access to the contained values.
                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                              Interaction
                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                              The member function is part of a group of related equal_range overloads within ara::core::Map:
                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                

                                                                                                                              • [SWS_CORE_01506]: Non-const variant for direct keys of type const key_type&.
                                                                                                                                • 

                                                                                                                              • [SWS_CORE_01507]: Const variant for direct keys of type const key_type&, which returns const_iterator.
                                                                                                                                • 

                                                                                                                              • [SWS_CORE_01509]: Const template overload for generic keys of type const K&.

                                                                                                                                      function erase [SWS_CORE_01480]
                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      iterator erase (iterator position);
                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      As per corresponding usage in [map]
                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      
  AI-GENERATED

  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 259948ff74a7
  Provenance
  

                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      
    The function erase of class ara::core::Map synchronously removes that element from the container that is referenced by the passed parameter position [SWS_CORE_01480]. The definition is included via header <ara/core/map.h> [SWS_CORE_01480]. As a return value, the function returns an iterator to the element of the map immediately following the removed element [SWS_CORE_01480]. The semantics follow the specification according to the corresponding usage in [map] [SWS_CORE_01480].
  
                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                      
    Regarding error handling, the operation is classified as not exception safe (not exception safe) [SWS_CORE_01480]. Specific error codes, fallback channels, or error notifications via DET or DEM are not specified for this call [SWS_CORE_01480]. Since the behavior is oriented towards [map], the passed iterator is likely to be invalidated by the erasing process, while iterators to remaining elements presumably remain intact [SWS_CORE_01480]. Passing an invalid or non-dereferenceable iterator presumably leads to undefined behavior due to lack of validation (Interpretation).
  
                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                      
    In interaction within ara::core::Map, alternative overloads exist: In addition to erasure via a mutable iterator, an overload for const_iterator is available [SWS_CORE_01481]. Likewise, elements can be removed key-based via key_type [SWS_CORE_01482] or as an entire iterator range [SWS_CORE_01483].

                                                                                                                                          The member function erase of class ara::core::Map serves for synchronous erasure of a single element at the position specified by iterator position [SWS_CORE_01481]. Declaration is done via header file ara/core/map.h [SWS_CORE_01481]. The behavior corresponds to the definition in [map], with the function returning a iterator to the succeeding element of the map [SWS_CORE_01481].
                                                                                                                                          
  
                                                                                                                                          Regarding exception handling, the function is specified as “not exception safe” [SWS_CORE_01481]. Specific error codes, violations, or error messages are not defined for this operation [SWS_CORE_01481]. Interpretation: Passing an invalid or non-dereferenceable iterator as position should lead to undefined behavior, as the specification does not provide for error checks.
                                                                                                                                          
  
                                                                                                                                          In interaction with the container interface of ara::core::Map, further overloads are available:
                                                                                                                                          
  
                                                                                                                                            
    
                                                                                                                                          • Erasure via a mutable iterator iterator position [SWS_CORE_01480],
                                                                                                                                            • 
    
                                                                                                                                          • Erasure by key via erase(const key_type &x) returning the number of removed elements [SWS_CORE_01482],
                                                                                                                                            • 
    
                                                                                                                                          • Range erasure via two iterators first and last [SWS_CORE_01483].
                                                                                                                                            • 
  
                                                                                                                                          
  
                                                                                                                                          Corresponding overloads for single const_iterator positions are analogously defined for other containers such as ara::core::Vector [SWS_CORE_01372] or ara::core::BasicString [SWS_CORE_03103].

                                                                                                                                              function erase [SWS_CORE_01482]
                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                              size_type erase (const key_type &x);
                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                              As per corresponding usage in [map]
                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                              
  AI-GENERATED
  unreviewed
  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 984e0b35e963
  Provenance
  

                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                              use
                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                              The synchronous member function erase of class ara::core::Map serves to remove entries via a specified key x of type const key_type& ([SWS_CORE_01482]). The interface is included via header ara/core/map.h. The functional behavior is defined as equivalent to usage in [map] ([SWS_CORE_01482]). Interpretation: According to this C++ standard reference, the return value of type size_type should indicate the number of elements successfully erased from the container.
                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                              Error Handling and Boundary Conditions
                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                              In the specification, the function is classified as not exception safe ([SWS_CORE_01482]). Specific return codes for error situations or reporting paths via DET or DEM are not defined for this container call. Interpretation: Due to the lack of exception safety, no guarantees regarding the state of the container should apply in the event of an error, which is why the caller should ensure consistent data and valid call parameters before execution.
                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                              Interaction
                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                              The method forms the key-based counterpart to the iterator-based erase operations of ara::core::Map, which clean up individual positions ([SWS_CORE_01480], [SWS_CORE_01481]) or closed iterator ranges ([SWS_CORE_01483]). The pattern of standardized erase functions is found across containers in ara::core, such as for ara::core::Vector ([SWS_CORE_01372]) or for ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03102]).

                                                                                                                                                  use
                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                  The member function erase of container ara::core::Map serves to remove a range of values delimited by two iterators [SWS_CORE_01483]. It is defined in header #include "ara/core/map.h" and has signature iterator erase (const_iterator first, const_iterator last); [SWS_CORE_01483]. Functionally, the behavior follows standard semantics in [map] [SWS_CORE_01483]. As a return value, it provides an iterator to the element immediately following the removed range, or the end of the container [SWS_CORE_01483].
                                                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                                                  Error Handling and Restrictions
                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                  The operation is explicitly classified in the specification as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_01483]. Specific AUTOSAR error codes or messages to DET or DEM are not defined for this function. The caller will therefore likely need to ensure on their own responsibility that first and last reference a valid, well-formed range within the same instance, as no separate checks are provided (interpretation).
                                                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                                                  Interaction
                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                  Within ara::core::Map, this range erase complements the overloads for removing single elements using iterator [SWS_CORE_01480], using const_iterator [SWS_CORE_01481], and by key key_type [SWS_CORE_01482]. Similar erase interfaces for iterator ranges can also be found in other containers of the Adaptive Core Library, namely in ara::core::Vector [SWS_CORE_01373] and ara::core::BasicString [SWS_CORE_03104].

                                                                                                                                                      function extract [SWS_CORE_01470]
                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      node_type extract (const_iterator position);
                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      As per corresponding usage in [map]
                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      
  AI-GENERATED
  unreviewed
  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 8c6034c84048
  Provenance
  

                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                      The member function extract of class ara::core::Map extracts the element at the position designated by iterator position and returns a node of type node_type [SWS_CORE_01470]. The declaration and semantics follow the corresponding usage in [map], whereby the node is extracted directly from the associative container. The function is provided via header ara/core/map.h.
                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                      Usage and Behavior
                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                      The call takes place synchronously on an instance of ara::core::Map. Passed as parameter is a const_iterator position, which, interpretation: must refer to a valid, dereferenceable element within the called map. Due to the extraction, the element is removed from the container, while the returned node_type object assumes ownership of the node.
                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                      Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                      Regarding exception handling, the function is explicitly classified as not exception safe according to the specification [SWS_CORE_01470]. If an exception occurs during execution, the operation guarantees no deterministic container guarantees, which is why calling code should provide appropriate safeguards.
                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                      Interaction and Alternatives
                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                      As an overload, alongside position-based extraction, the key-based variant extract(const key_type &x) is also available [SWS_CORE_01471]. The latter allows extracting an entry directly based on its key value, without having to determine an iterator manually beforehand.

                                                                                                                                                          use
                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                          The synchronous member function extract is defined in header file #include "ara/core/map.h" within class ara::core::Map [SWS_CORE_01471]. It accepts a constant key reference const key_type &x as a parameter and returns the found element as node_type [SWS_CORE_01471]. The functional semantics refer to the corresponding usage in [map] [SWS_CORE_01471]; this likely corresponds to the C++ standard according to which the node is extracted directly from the container without having to copy key or value.
                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                          Error Handling and Restrictions
                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                          The function is explicitly classified as \u201cnot exception safe\u201d in the specification [SWS_CORE_01471]. Specific error codes, error classes, or DET or DEM notifications are not defined in the payload. In the event of an error, there are therefore likely no guarantees regarding the preservation or consistency of the container state, which is why calling code should provide appropriate protective measures.
                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                          Interaction
                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                          The specification element directly relates to the overload node_type extract(const_iterator position) [SWS_CORE_01470]. While the present function identifies and extracts an element via the search key [SWS_CORE_01471], the related variant enables targeted extraction via an already known iterator position [SWS_CORE_01470]. Both interfaces belong to the scope of ara::core::Map and share the same property of lacking exception safety [SWS_CORE_01470] [SWS_CORE_01471].

                                                                                                                                                              iterator find (const key_type &x);
