  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: a5eb50f4008c
  Provenance
  

                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                              use
                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                              The member function find of class ara::core::Map is used to find an element synchronously using its key [SWS_CORE_01490]. The function is declared in header file ara/core/map.h. It takes a reference to the sought key (const key_type &x) and returns a mutable iterator to the found key-value pair; if no matching entry is found, the return corresponds to the end iterator of the map [SWS_CORE_01490].
                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                              Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                              According to the specification, this function is classified as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_01490]. Error notifications via DET or DEM are not specified for this basic container service. If operational errors occur during comparison, exceptions of the underlying comparison operator can be propagated.
                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                              Concurrency and Interaction
                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                              Since this is a non-const member function that returns a writable iterator, concurrent access without synchronization is presumably not thread-safe. For purely read access to const instances of ara::core::Map, the overload with const_iterator is available [SWS_CORE_01491]. In addition, templated overloads support transparent lookup with compatible comparison types K, both modifying [SWS_CORE_01492] and const [SWS_CORE_01493]. In contrast to the character-based find functions in ara::core::StringView [SWS_CORE_02157] or ara::core::BasicString [SWS_CORE_03315], which return indices of type size_type and are partly noexcept, this function operates container-based via iterators.

                                                                                                                                                                  const_iterator find (const key_type &x) const;

  Provenance
  

                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                  The const member function find of class ara::core::Map serves to synchronously find an entry by its key [SWS_CORE_01491]. Header #include "ara/core/map.h" must be included for the call. The function expects a reference to the searched key const key_type &x as a parameter. The behavior corresponds to the specification of [map] in the C++ standard, so that upon a successful search a const_iterator to the element is returned, and otherwise end() is presumably returned [SWS_CORE_01491].
                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                  Regarding error handling, the function is declared as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_01491]. Since the search operation is based on comparing keys, exceptions that occur are likely to result primarily from the user-defined comparison operation. No DET or DEM error messages are defined for this elementary container. Since this is a read-only operation on a const instance, concurrent access by multiple threads to the same object can be parallelized according to standard C++ container semantics, as long as no simultaneous modifications take place (interpretation).
                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                  In interplay with other interfaces, the method complements the non-const variant [SWS_CORE_01490], which returns a modifiable iterator. For heterogeneous search operations without type conversion, template overloads for modifiable [SWS_CORE_01492] as well as constant instances [SWS_CORE_01493] are also available in ara::core::Map. Search functions of the same name also exist in the Core module for string classes such as ara::core::BasicString [SWS_CORE_03407] and ara::core::StringView [SWS_CORE_02157].

                                                                                                                                                                      The template member function find according to [SWS_CORE_01492] serves to synchronously find an element within an instance of ara::core::Map via header file ara/core/map.h. It accepts a reference parameter const K &x and returns a mutable iterator to the found key-value pair or the container's end iterator. The specification refers to the behavior of [map]; the generic parameter form is likely to be interpreted here as a heterogeneous key search in order to compare search keys of differing types without prior conversion.
                                                                                                                                                                      

  
                                                                                                                                                                      Regarding error handling and exception safety, the function is explicitly classified as not exception safe ([SWS_CORE_01492]). Specific error codes, return values for error states, or DET/DEM messages are not defined in the payload. If an exception occurs during comparison or internal traversal, the call offers no exception guarantee.
                                                                                                                                                                      

  
                                                                                                                                                                      In the interplay within ara::core::Map, the function forms the non-const counterpart to the const heterogeneous search [SWS_CORE_01493] as well as to the non-generic overloads [SWS_CORE_01490] and [SWS_CORE_01491], each of which is tied firmly to const key_type &x. It differs fundamentally from the identically named search functions of other containers, such as ara::core::StringView ([SWS_CORE_02157]) or ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03315]), which perform string-based position searches and are partially declared as noexcept.

                                                                                                                                                                          • It complements the non-const template variant iterator find(const K &x) [SWS_CORE_01492].
                                                                                                                                                                            • 

                                                                                                                                                                          • It forms the generic counterpart to the overloads with fixed const key_type &x, which are declared as non-const [SWS_CORE_01490] and const [SWS_CORE_01491].
                                                                                                                                                                            • 

                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                          It thus differs from the operations of the same name in ara::core::StringView (e.g. [SWS_CORE_02157]) and ara::core::BasicString (e.g. [SWS_CORE_03315]), which operate on strings, return positions of type size_type, and are declared as exception safe.
                                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                          This usage note was generated by an AI based on AUTOSAR specification R25-11.

                                                                                                                                                                                  function insert [SWS_CORE_01460]
                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                  std::pair< iterator, bool > insert (const value_type &x);
                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                  As per corresponding usage in [map]

  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: f9d1b30a5cc8
  Provenance
  

                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                  use
                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                  The function insert in the context of ara::core::Map serves to synchronously add a value element by copy via the parameter const value_type &x ([SWS_CORE_01460]). The operation is included via the header file ara/core/map.h. The return type std::pair<iterator, bool> follows the specification “As per corresponding usage in [map]”: Interpretation: Here, the iterator likely refers to the newly inserted or already existing element, while the boolean flag indicates successful new insertion.
                                                                                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                                                                                  Error handling
                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                  No specific AUTOSAR error codes such as DET or DEM messages are provided in the specification. The function is explicitly declared as not exception safe (“not exception safe”) ([SWS_CORE_01460]). If an internal memory allocation or copying of the element fails, the container provides no exception or rollback guarantees; such an error would presumably lead to termination or an undefined state.
                                                                                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                                                                                  Concurrency and Limitations
                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                  The call occurs synchronously in the thread of the caller. The container operations do not have integrated synchronization, which is why the function is not reentrant with respect to the same instance. Concurrent read or write accesses must be protected by the caller.
                                                                                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                                                                                  Interaction
                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                  Complementary overloads of insert exist for ara::core::Map:
                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                    

                                                                                                                                                                                  • Move-based variants for temporary values ([SWS_CORE_01461], [SWS_CORE_01462]),
                                                                                                                                                                                    • 

                                                                                                                                                                                  • Position-based insert operations with iterator hint ([SWS_CORE_01463], [SWS_CORE_01464]),
                                                                                                                                                                                    • 

                                                                                                                                                                                  • Range and initializer lists ([SWS_CORE_01466], [SWS_CORE_01467]) as well as node-handle transfers ([SWS_CORE_01468], [SWS_CORE_01469]).
                                                                                                                                                                                    • 

                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                  Analogous insert operations are found with adapted signatures in other Core classes such as ara::core::Vector ([SWS_CORE_01367]) and ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03093]).

                                                                                                                                                                                      The member function insert of ara::core::Map synchronously inserts an element into the associative container via move semantics using an rvalue reference (value_type &&x) ([SWS_CORE_01461]). Declaration is provided via header file #include "ara/core/map.h" ([SWS_CORE_01461]). According to the specification, functional behavior complies with the corresponding usage in [map] of the C++ standard ([SWS_CORE_01461]). The function returns a std::pair<iterator, bool>; interpretation: here, the boolean value is likely to indicate whether the element was newly inserted, while the iterator points to the element in the container ([SWS_CORE_01461]).
                                                                                                                                                                                      

  
                                                                                                                                                                                      Regarding error handling and exception safety, the function is explicitly classified in the specification as not exception safe ([SWS_CORE_01461]). Specific error codes or AUTOSAR error messages like DET or DEM are not specified for this call.
                                                                                                                                                                                      

  
                                                                                                                                                                                      In the interaction within ara::core::Map, this overload represents the rvalue-based counterpart to the copy variant insert(const value_type &) ([SWS_CORE_01460]) and the generic template version insert(P &&) ([SWS_CORE_01462]). For insertions with a position hint, overloads with a hint iterator such as insert(const_iterator, value_type &&) ([SWS_CORE_01464]) and for node handles via insert(node_type &&) ([SWS_CORE_01468]) using insert_return_type ([SWS_CORE_01418]) are also available.

                                                                                                                                                                                          function insert [SWS_CORE_01462]
                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                          template <class P> std::pair< iterator, bool > insert (P &&x);

                                                                                                                                                                                          Template member function insert of class ara::core::Map serves to synchronously insert a compatible key-value pair via a forwarding reference P&& x into the associative container instance [SWS_CORE_01462]. It is included via header #include "ara/core/map.h" and references the semantics of [map] [SWS_CORE_01462] for its behavior. As return value, it delivers a std::pair<iterator, bool> [SWS_CORE_01462]. Interpretation: The boolean return value is expected to signal whether a new entry was created, while the iterator points to the newly inserted or already existing element.
                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                          Regarding error handling, the function is expressly categorized in the specification as not exception safe (not exception safe) [SWS_CORE_01462]. Specific error codes, error messages, or interfaces to diagnostic and error memories such as DET or DEM are not specified for this call.
                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                          Regarding concurrency and constraints, the call modifies the state of the map; therefore, concurrent access to the same instance is presumably not reentrant and requires external protection against data races. Execution takes place synchronously in the context of the calling thread.
                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                          In interplay within ara::core::Map, this generic function complements the direct overloads for const value_type& [SWS_CORE_01460] and value_type&& [SWS_CORE_01461]. In addition, position-based insert operations with iterator hint [SWS_CORE_01465], range operations [SWS_CORE_01466], and the insertion of node handles via insert_return_type [SWS_CORE_01418] [SWS_CORE_01468] exist.

                                                                                                                                                                                              use
                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                              Synchronous member function insert of ara::core::Map inserts an element by copy via const reference x of type value_type into the associative container [SWS_CORE_01463]. Parameter position presumably serves as a position hint (hint) to find the insertion position within the ordered structure more efficiently, as suggested by the reference to [map]. As return value, the function provides a iterator pointing to the newly inserted element or to the element already present with the same key.
                                                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                                                              Restrictions and Error Handling
                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                              Exception safety is explicitly not specified for the operation (not exception safe) [SWS_CORE_01463]. If, for example, internal memory allocation or creation of the key-value pair fails, no guarantees regarding restoration of a consistent state are expected to take effect. Specific error codes, return values for error states, or mechanisms such as DET and DEM are not provided in the specification.
                                                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                                                              Interaction
                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                              The method is part of the overload family for insertion operations in ara::core::Map. Besides this copy variant with hint, rvalue-based overloads with [SWS_CORE_01464], generic variants [SWS_CORE_01465], and hint insertions for node handles [SWS_CORE_01469] are available. If no position hint is passed, insert signals insertion success via a std::pair<iterator, bool> [SWS_CORE_01460], [SWS_CORE_01461], [SWS_CORE_01462], or returns type insert_return_type [SWS_CORE_01418] for node moves [SWS_CORE_01468].

                                                                                                                                                                                                  function insert [SWS_CORE_01464]

                                                                                                                                                                                                  use
                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                  Member function insert of ara::core::Map ([SWS_CORE_01464]) inserts an rvalue element synchronously into the map. The call is made via header #include "ara/core/map.h". The interface accepts a position iterator position of type const_iterator as well as the element x to be taken over via move semantics (value_type &&). As return value, it delivers a iterator pointing to the inserted element or the element already present in the container with an equivalent key. Interpretation: Parameter position is expected to serve as an insertion hint that, according to the semantics of [map], can reduce the search effort in the tree when optimally placed.
                                                                                                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                                                                                                  Error Handling and Concurrency
                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                  The specification explicitly identifies the function as "not exception safe" ([SWS_CORE_01464]). Specific error codes, return statuses for error notification, or DET/DEM reports do not exist. If a memory allocation or moving of the object data fails, the implementation presumably offers no assurance of a consistent state. Concurrent calls on the same instance are not protected; concurrent access requires external synchronization by the caller.
                                                                                                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                                                                                                  Interaction
                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                  Within ara::core::Map, the function complements the lvalue overload with position [SWS_CORE_01463] as well as generic forwarding [SWS_CORE_01465]. While the hintless overloads [SWS_CORE_01460] and [SWS_CORE_01461] return a std::pair<iterator, bool> to provide information about the actual insertion process, this function returns only the iterator. For node-based moves, [SWS_CORE_01469] also provides a hint variant for node_type &&.

                                                                                                                                                                                                      The template member function insert of container ara::core::Map inserts an element synchronously using a position hint [SWS_CORE_01465]. The function is defined in header file #include "ara/core/map.h" and takes a position iterator position of type const_iterator as well as a universal reference parameter P && [SWS_CORE_01465]. As return value, it returns a iterator [SWS_CORE_01465].
                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                      Regarding the exact behavior, the specification refers to the corresponding usage in [map] [SWS_CORE_01465]. Interpretation: The parameter position should serve as a search hint that accelerates the insertion operation if placed correctly, while the passed value is perfectly forwarded by means of P &&. Interpretation: A new element should only be inserted if no element with an equivalent key already exists; the returned iterator presumably points to the newly inserted or already existing key-value pair.
                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                      Regarding error handling and robustness, the function is explicitly classified in the specification as “not exception safe” [SWS_CORE_01465]. Specific error codes, AUTOSAR return values via ara::core::Result, or mechanisms such as DET/DEM are not provided for this operation.
                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                      Within ara::core::Map, this function complements related insert operations, including the overload for generic types without position hint [SWS_CORE_01462], overloads with hint for value_type [SWS_CORE_01463], [SWS_CORE_01464], and the reinsertion of node structures by means of node_type [SWS_CORE_01469].

                                                                                                                                                                                                          The template function insert of class ara::core::Map inserts a sequence of elements from the range specified by the input iterators [first, last) into the container [SWS_CORE_01466]. According to the specification, the behavior corresponds to standard usage in std::map, where the operation executes synchronously and returns no value (void) [SWS_CORE_01466]. The function is provided via header <ara/core/map.h> [SWS_CORE_01466].
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                          Regarding error handling, range insertion is explicitly classified as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_01466]. Specific error codes or error hooks such as DET or DEM messages are not provided within the scope of the specification. Interpretation: If errors or exceptions occur during the insertion of elements, the state of the container should remain inconsistent and no rollback of already inserted elements presumably takes place.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                          In interaction with other interfaces of ara::core::Map, this function serves for range population. It complements the overloads for inserting individual values via copy or move semantics ([SWS_CORE_01460], [SWS_CORE_01461]) as well as inserting fixed sets of values via std::initializer_list [SWS_CORE_01467] or node handles [SWS_CORE_01468].

                                                                                                                                                                                                              The member function insert of class ara::core::Map ([SWS_CORE_01467], header file ara/core/map.h) enables the synchronous insertion of multiple elements via a std::initializer_list<value_type>. The function has no return value (void). According to the specification, the behavior follows the corresponding usage in [map] ([SWS_CORE_01467]); Interpretation: Key-value pairs whose keys already exist in the map are likely to remain unchanged and not be overwritten.
                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                              Neither specific error codes nor notifications to DET or DEM are defined for this call. Regarding exception handling, the operation is expressly declared as not exception safe ([SWS_CORE_01467]). If an error occurs during the insertion process, such as a failed memory allocation, the function presumably provides no rollback guarantee for already inserted elements. Furthermore, reentrancy commitments are absent; concurrent accesses to the same instance must be synchronized externally by the caller.
                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                              In the interaction of the interfaces of ara::core::Map, this function complements the iterator-based range overload insert(InputIterator, InputIterator) ([SWS_CORE_01466]) as well as single-value insertions with boolean success feedback ([SWS_CORE_01460], [SWS_CORE_01461], [SWS_CORE_01462]), positional hints ([SWS_CORE_01463], [SWS_CORE_01464], [SWS_CORE_01465]), and node handles ([SWS_CORE_01468], [SWS_CORE_01469]). In ara::core::Vector, a comparable overload for initializer lists exists with [SWS_CORE_01371].

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The member function insert of ara::core::Map serves to insert an existing node handle (node_type &&nh) into the associative container [SWS_CORE_01468]. The return type is insert_return_type, which is specified according to [SWS_CORE_01418] as an implementation-defined type via iterator and node type ({<insert-return-type>}<iterator, node_type>). The call is synchronous and is provided via the header file #include "ara/core/map.h" [SWS_CORE_01468].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Regarding error behavior, the function is classified as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_01468]. Specific error codes via ara::core::Result or DET/DEM messages are not defined in the specification. Due to the normative reference to the standard behavior in [map], the operation is likely not to insert the passed node in the event of a key conflict, but rather to reflect its state in the returned insert_return_type.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  In interaction with other interfaces of ara::core::Map, this overload represents a resource-saving node adoption: Alternatively, a node can be inserted with a search hint via insert(const_iterator hint, node_type &&nh) [SWS_CORE_01469]. For regular value pairs, overloads via copy or move of value_type returning a std::pair<iterator, bool> are available [SWS_CORE_01460] [SWS_CORE_01461], as well as overloads for iterator ranges [SWS_CORE_01466] and initializer lists [SWS_CORE_01467]. In the absence of explicit synchronization guarantees in the requirements, a concurrent call on the same container instance is likely not thread-safe.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      function insert [SWS_CORE_01469]

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      use
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The synchronous member function insert from header ara/core/map.h is used to insert an existing node handle into an instance of ara::core::Map using a position hint ([SWS_CORE_01469]). The function accepts a const_iterator hint as a suggestion for the insertion position as well as an rvalue handle nh of type node_type&& and returns a iterator to the element ([SWS_CORE_01469]). The behavior corresponds to the specification of std::map ([SWS_CORE_01469]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Error Handling and Exception Behavior
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The operation is explicitly classified as not exception safe (not exception safe) ([SWS_CORE_01469]). Specific error codes, DET/DEM messages, or return values for error indication are not defined in the payload. In the event of an error or allocation problems, the state of the container and node is likely to remain Interpretation: potentially inconsistent.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Concurrency and Limitations
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The call is synchronous. Synchronization mechanisms are not specified, which is why concurrent access by multiple execution contexts to the same map instance is presumably not thread-safe. Due to the rvalue semantics, the passed node is transferred into the data structure upon successful insertion.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Interaction
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The function complements the node-based insertion operations of ara::core::Map: In contrast to the overload without position specification ([SWS_CORE_01468]), which returns a insert_return_type ([SWS_CORE_01418]), this variant directly returns a iterator ([SWS_CORE_01469]). Further overloads allow the insertion of value pairs with a position specification ([SWS_CORE_01463], [SWS_CORE_01464], [SWS_CORE_01465]) or without a position specification ([SWS_CORE_01460], [SWS_CORE_01461], [SWS_CORE_01462]).

The behavior complies with the corresponding usage in [map] [SWS_CORE_01476].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The function takes the key as a const reference const key_type &k as well as the object to be assigned as a forwarding reference M &&obj and returns a std::pair<iterator, bool> [SWS_CORE_01476]. Interpretation: The resulting pair is likely to refer to the inserted or updated element and indicate via the boolean value whether an insertion actually took place [SWS_CORE_01476].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Regarding error handling and robustness, the function is specified as not exception safe (not exception safe) [SWS_CORE_01476]. In the event of an error or if exceptions occur during assignment or allocation, the container thus does not guarantee a consistent state.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          In interaction with other interfaces, ara::core::Map provides alternative overloads:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              use
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The template member function insert_or_assign belongs to class ara::core::Map and is provided via header file ara/core/map.h [SWS_CORE_01477]. It accepts the key k as an rvalue reference (key_type&&) and moves it if necessary. The assigned value obj is passed as a universal reference (M&&). The behavior corresponds to standard map semantics: If the key is already present, the associated value is updated; otherwise, a new key-value pair is inserted. As a return value, the synchronous function returns a std::pair<iterator, bool> containing an iterator to the element as well as a flag indicating whether an actual new insertion occurred [SWS_CORE_01477].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Error Handling and Concurrency
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              In the specification, the function is expressly classified as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_01477]. Neither specific error codes nor notifications to DET or DEM are defined. If a memory allocation or a value assignment fails, the internal state of the map is likely to potentially remain inconsistent. Likewise, concurrent accesses by multiple threads to the same container instance without external synchronization are likely not thread-safe.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Interaction
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The operation is part of a family of overloads in ara::core::Map:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • If the key must be preserved as a reference, the overload with const key_type& according to [SWS_CORE_01476] is available.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • 
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • For targeted insertions with a position hint (const_iterator hint), the variants [SWS_CORE_01478] (constant key) and [SWS_CORE_01479] (rvalue key) offer hint-based calls that directly return a iterator.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                •

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  function insert_or_assign [SWS_CORE_01478]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  template <class M> iterator insert_or_assign (const_iterator hint, const key_type &k, M &&obj);
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  As per corresponding usage in [map]

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  use
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The function insert_or_assign of class ara::core::Map synchronously inserts an element with the constant key k and the value obj or updates an existing mapping [SWS_CORE_01478]. The signature accepts as parameters a position hint const_iterator hint, the key const key_type &k, and the object to be forwarded M &&obj, and returns a iterator to the inserted or updated element [SWS_CORE_01478]. The behavior is specified as “As per corresponding usage in [map]”; the iterator hint is likely to serve as an optimization hint for the insertion position [SWS_CORE_01478].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Error Handling and Boundary Conditions
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  For this function, exception safety is explicitly defined as “not exception safe” [SWS_CORE_01478]. Specific error codes or mechanisms such as DET or DEM are not provided for in the specification. If an exception occurs during assignment or memory allocation, the data structure is therefore likely not to remain in any guaranteed consistent state.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Interaction
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The operation is defined in header <ara/core/map.h> for ara::core::Map [SWS_CORE_01478] and is accompanied by related overloads:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • [SWS_CORE_01476] accepts const key_type &k without a position hint and returns std::pair<iterator, bool>.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • [SWS_CORE_01477] accepts key_type &&k via move semantics without a position hint and returns std::pair<iterator, bool>.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • [SWS_CORE_01479] likewise accepts a const_iterator hint, but binds the key as an rvalue key_type &&k and returns a iterator.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    •

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      function insert_or_assign [SWS_CORE_01479]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      template <class M> iterator insert_or_assign (const_iterator hint, key_type &&k, M &&obj);

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The template member function insert_or_assign of class ara::core::Map ([SWS_CORE_01479]) serves to insert a key-value pair or update an existing entry. Access is provided via header file #include "ara/core/map.h" [SWS_CORE_01479].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The overload accepts three parameters [SWS_CORE_01479]:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • hint (const_iterator): Interpretation: According to the specification “As per corresponding usage in [map]”, this iterator is likely to serve as a position hint to speed up the insertion process.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • 
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • k (key_type&&): The key to be moved.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • 
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • obj (M&&): The value to be assigned as a universal reference.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • 
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      As a return value, the function returns a iterator to the inserted or updated element [SWS_CORE_01479]. In contrast to the overloads without a search hint [SWS_CORE_01476], [SWS_CORE_01477], which return a std::pair<iterator, bool>, no boolean status is transmitted here.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The specification expressly declares the operation as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_01479]. Specific AUTOSAR error codes, DET, or DEM messages are not defined in the payload. Due to the lack of synchronization guarantees, the function is likely not thread-safe against concurrent accesses. Together with the variant for constant lvalue keys [SWS_CORE_01478], it completes the container's hint-based insertion operations.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          function key_comp [SWS_CORE_01488]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          key_compare key_comp () const;
